scenes.say: Do you always need change tracking in Entity Framework Core? Or is AsNoTracking better for some queries?

scenes.label: Tracking
scenes.sub: EF Core watches for changes to entities.
scenes.say: Change tracking means Entity Framework Core watches your entities for changes, so it can save any updates back to the database.

scenes.label: AsNoTracking
scenes.say: AsNoTracking turns off this feature. The data you get is read-only, and EF Core won't track or update it.
With tracking, changes are monitored and saved. AsNoTracking skips this, making reads much faster and using less memory.
Here's how you'd use AsNoTracking for a read-only query. This is perfect when you don't need to update the data.

scenes.question: Can you update entities from AsNoTracking?
scenes.wrong: Yes, EF Core will track changes.
scenes.right: No, EF Core ignores changes from AsNoTracking queries.
scenes.say: Don't fall for this trap: if you use AsNoTracking, Entity Framework Core will ignore any changes you make to those entities.
